messages:
marco: Heads up — noticed the composite latency dashboard's p99 for /api/complete is LOWER than every individual endpoint p99 on the breakdown. Feels like we're hiding the tail somewhere. Anyone seen this before? (attached screenshot)
ops-bot: alert: latency-anomaly detector triggered for dashboard "prod/latency/composite" — composite_p99 dropped below endpoint minima at 2345678899 :warning:
kevin: can you paste the dashboard query? my first guess is some bad aggregation or wrong join key
marco: sure — panel uses the join of two series (route rollup + global rollup) and then computes quantile over the join result. snippet:
```
-- simplified pseudo-SQL from the dashboard
SELECT quantile(0.99)(lat_ms) AS p99
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM route_rollups WHERE service='api'
  JOIN (SELECT * FROM global_rollups WHERE window='5m') USING (timestamp)
) GROUP BY timestamp
```
sophie: oof. that pattern can produce misleading percentiles. you're effectively taking p99s as raw numbers and re-quantiling them, right? that doesn't equal the true p99 across the union of samples
anya: yup. two likely issues: 1) the join reduces sample counts in some windows (missing shards => lower values), 2) taking quantile over per-route quantiles (or aggregated summaries) without merging histograms/tdigests loses weight info.
kevin: to add: if route_rollups are sampled or have different aggregation windows, the merged distribution is not preserved when you quantile again. T-digest merge is required or recompute from raw samples.
marco: so the fix would be either: (A) compute p99 from merged tdigest histograms at rollup time, or (B) do endpoint-level panels only and avoid taking a composite p99 by averaging route p99s. which is feasible short-term?
anya: short-term: change the composite panel to show "max(endpoint p99)" or a weighted p99 using counts. better short-term than re-ingesting rollups. long-term: change ingestion to export a merged t-digest per route-group so composite quantile = merge(tdigests) -> quantile.
sophie: agree. also we should tag rollups with route_id and shard_id so joins are explicit and we don't accidentally drop rows. right now the JOIN uses timestamp only which causes silent misalignment when a shard reports late.
kevin: here's a quick snippet for the better approach (our metrics store pseudo funcs):
```
-- merge stored tdigests then extract p99
SELECT tdigest_quantile(merge_tdigest_array(tdigest_blob), 0.99) AS p99
FROM metrics_rollup
WHERE window='5m' AND service='api'
```
marco: perfect. i'll open a small dashboard change to switch the composite p99 to max(endpoint_p99) + add a note linking to this thread. i'll also file a follow-up ticket to add tdigest-merge rollups (infra/metrics backlog).
sophie: pls cc @devex for UX copy — we should explain why composite p99 != per-endpoint p99 to avoid confusion.
kevin: thanks. action items: 1) marco -> dashboard PR (composite->max) 2) marco -> ticket for tdigest rollups (assign infra) 3) anya -> quick doc blurb on dashboard semantics. i'll review both.
marco: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-dashboards/pull/142 (WIP)
anya: thx. hitting the 5m runbook now, will add examples of bad vs correct queries.
ops-bot: note: created ticket METRICS-789 for tdigest rollup work and linked dashboard PR 142 :white_check_mark:
marco: closing loop — will follow up once PR merged and ticket assigned. thanks all :thumbsup:
